$comment: Campaign principles extracted from existing project documentation. Every entry carries a real source reference that can be checked. Classification is deliberately conservative: 'verified' is used ONLY where the source states a measured figure or a confirmed system behaviour. Nothing here was invented to fill a gap, and no evidence has been manufactured — where a principle is a judgement call, it is classified 'hypothesis' and says so.

classificationRules.verified: Source states a measured number, a confirmed backend/system behaviour, or an application rule that is enforced in code today.
classificationRules.observation: Source records a decision or a repeatedly-applied practice, but without measured evidence that it improves outcomes.
classificationRules.hypothesis: Reasonable design judgement with no supporting evidence in any source. Must not be presented as established.

principles.statement: There is no campaign performance history for this bank. Do not state or assume a conversion rate, and do not design around one. Size the audience and set expectations from what the manager tells you, and say plainly that the first run establishes the baseline.
principles.implication: A single campaign rarely produces enough conversions to support a confident conclusion. Do not promise lift.

principles.statement: No booked-conversion rate exists for this bank either. A number here would be invented, so do not quote one. Report what the campaign would have to produce to be worth running, and let the first run measure it.
principles.implication: Funnel expectations should be set against the addressable base, not against the engaged subset.

principles.statement: An auth-triggered EMI request stays open for up to 7 days before it is marked Expired. A campaign waiting on that outcome should not time out sooner.
principles.evidence: Reconciliation waits up to 7 days before marking a request Expired, to buffer past slower-than-T+1 settlement cases.
principles.implication: Use a 7-day timeout on a Wait for Event node awaiting EMI resolution.

principles.statement: Customer cooldown and quiet hours are real, implemented guardrails. A maximum-messages-per-day cap and a cooldown override are NOT implemented and must not be assumed available.
principles.evidence: Audit found cooldown and quiet hours present in the Frequency Limits step; max-per-day and cooldown-override were documented but never built, and were moved to out-of-scope.
principles.implication: Do not design a campaign that depends on a per-day cap being enforced by the platform.

principles.statement: Change one major variable per experiment so an observed difference can be attributed to a specific change.
principles.evidence: Stated as a design requirement in the agentic concept note. No measured evidence in any source that multi-variable campaigns actually produced unattributable results here.
principles.source: Agentic Drip Campaign concept note, 2026-10-12 (Key Considerations)
principles.implication: Prefer a single Experiment node varying one thing.

principles.statement: A campaign claiming incremental lift needs a holdout. Without a control group the result cannot be separated from what would have happened anyway.
principles.evidence: controlPct exists as a first-class campaign field and seed campaigns use 0/5/10%. No measured evidence recorded for which value is correct.
principles.implication: Set a non-zero controlPct when the goal is framed as incremental.

principles.statement: Independent time-based checkpoints from one anchor are parallel paths, not a routed choice — every customer passes every checkpoint.
principles.evidence: Encoded in the application as the routing-vs-fan-out rule (dcCanFanOut / dcIsRoutingNode) and enforced in three places including analytics counting.
principles.implication: Use fan-out from the entry node; do not model checkpoints as Branch arms.

principles.statement: Check the campaign goal after a message or wait, and stop messaging a customer who has already achieved it.
principles.evidence: The application auto-inserts a Goal Check after every Send and Wait whenever a campaign Goal is defined, wiring Yes to Goal Reached.
principles.appliesTo: any campaign with a defined Goal
principles.implication: Define a Goal so the platform inserts these automatically rather than hand-building checks.

principles.statement: A fallback channel on a Send is for delivery failure on the primary channel. It is a property of one Send, not a separate step.
principles.evidence: Channel Failover was folded into Send as an optional fallbackChannel; it is no longer a node type.
principles.implication: Configure fallback inside the Send, not as a chained node.

principles.statement: Do not lead with email because it is the cheapest channel. For Indian retail cardholders WhatsApp and in-app are read where email is not, so choose the first touch on reach and on where the customer can act, not on cost per message. Cost is a tie-breaker between channels that would both work, never the reason to pick the first one.
principles.source: No supporting source. Recorded as a hypothesis so it is not mistaken for established practice.
principles.implication: May inform a suggestion, but must be stated as an assumption, never as a reason the campaign will perform better.

principles.statement: Do not repeat on a fixed clock. Forty-eight hours is a guard against nagging, not a rhythm to design to: the same day is fine when someone has just opened or clicked and is still in the moment, and a longer gap is right when nothing has happened. Respect the night quiet hours. The test is whether another message is useful to them, not whether enough time has passed.
principles.source: No supporting source. Mock value lives in agent-proto/context/bank-context.json and is labelled INVENTED.
principles.implication: Spacing is a judgement call on each send, not a constraint to comply with. The night quiet hours are the real limit. Decide the gap from what the customer has just done and say why you chose it.

knownGaps: No campaign performance data exists anywhere in this project, so no principle here is backed by a measured outcome of a shipped campaign.
No principle has been validated against the fictional Meridian Bank, which has no history at all.
No campaign performance history for this bank. No conversion rate, no benchmark, no prior-campaign learning. The first run establishes the baseline.
